newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cabinet approves television decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy cabinet approves television decree.

text.p: The Italian cabinet on Wednesday granted a reprieve for media mogul Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset television empire with a decree extending the current legal framework for television stations until January 31, 1997.

The decree plugs a legal void in which magistrates could have forced the former prime minister to take one of the three stations he controls off the air because of a court ruling that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three channels.
Government sources said the decree contained only the five-month extension and no anti-trust measures, as Post and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico had been reported to want.
Italy's constitutional court handed down the ruling in December 1994 and set midnight on August 27, 1996 as the deadline for a new legal framework.

The deadline passed without incident after a day of ministerial meetings to hammer out a compromise, giving parliament breathing space to enact new legislation, presented by the government in July, covering the broadcast sector.
If passed into law, Prime Minister Romano Prodi's proposed bill would force Mediaset to convert one of its three networks into a satellite or cable station by August 1997.
